channel.title: Weekly Menu
channel.description: Heart-healthy weekday dinners. No shellfish. No yoghurt. No eggs.

item.title: Monday — Vietnamese Lemongrass Chicken Bowl (bún gà nướng)
item.description:
Serves 2. Marinate ahead if you can — the bowl pays you back.

Ingredients

  • 2 skinless chicken breasts (~300g), sliced thin
  • 2 stalks lemongrass, white parts only, finely minced
  • 2 garlic cloves, grated
  • 1 tbsp fish sauce (low-sodium if available)
  • 1 tsp honey
  • 1 tbsp neutral oil + ½ tsp turmeric (optional, for color)
  • Black pepper
  • 200g rice vermicelli, dry
  • 1 cucumber, julienned
  • 1 carrot, julienned
  • Big handfuls fresh mint and cilantro
  • 1 head butter or romaine lettuce, torn
  • Bean sprouts (optional)

Nuoc cham: 2 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tsp honey, 1 grated garlic clove, 1 minced bird's eye chili, 4 tbsp water

Method

  1. Mix lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, honey, oil, turmeric, and pepper. Toss with chicken. Marinate 20 min (or up to overnight).
  2. Soak vermicelli in just-boiled water 4–5 min until tender. Drain, rinse cold.
  3. Whisk nuoc cham. Should taste sour-salty-sweet-hot, in that order.
  4. Heat a non-stick pan or grill pan hot. Cook chicken 2–3 min per side until charred at the edges and just cooked through.
  5. Build bowls: noodles, lettuce, herbs, cucumber, carrot, sprouts, chicken on top. Pour over the nuoc cham at the table.

Tip: If you can find Thai basil, throw that in too. The fresh herbs aren't garnish — they're the dish.

item.title: Tuesday — Moroccan Chickpea & Harissa Stew
item.description:
Serves 4 — leftovers reheat brilliantly. Make Tuesday for Wednesday's lunch.

Ingredients

  • 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 yellow onion, diced
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • 1 tsp ground coriander
  • Pinch of cinnamon
  • 1–2 tbsp harissa paste (start with 1)
  • 1 × 400g can chopped tomatoes
  • 2 × 400g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed (no-salt-added if available)
  • 250ml low-sodium vegetable stock
  • ¼ preserved lemon, finely chopped (optional but worth it)
  • Big handful flat-leaf parsley, chopped
  • Lemon wedges, to serve

Method

  1. Olive oil into a deep pan over medium. Onion, soft and translucent, ~6 min.
  2. Garlic and dry spices in. Stir 30 seconds — toasted, not burnt.
  3. Harissa, tomatoes, chickpeas, stock. Bring to a simmer. Lid askew, 20 min, stirring now and then. Should thicken into something stew-like.
  4. Stir in preserved lemon. Taste before salting — preserved lemon brings its own. Off the heat.
  5. Pile parsley on top. Lemon wedge on the side. Eat with whole-grain couscous or just a hunk of good bread.

Tip: Day-two version is better than day one.

item.title: Wednesday — Miso-Glazed Salmon with Sesame Greens
item.description:
Serves 2. Twenty minutes start to finish.

Ingredients

  • 2 salmon fillets, skin-on (~150g each)
  • Glaze: 1 tbsp white miso, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tsp low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tsp grated ginger, ½ tsp toasted sesame oil
  • 2 heads bok choy, halved lengthwise (or 200g spinach)
  • 1 garlic clove, sliced thin
  • 1 tsp neutral oil
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
  • Splash of low-sodium soy
  • Steamed brown rice, to serve (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat broiler/grill to high. Whisk glaze. Pat salmon dry, brush glaze on top.
  2. Line a tray with foil. Salmon skin-down. Broil 6–8 min — glaze should bubble and char in spots; flesh should flake but stay just translucent in the center.
  3. Meanwhile: oil in a wide pan over medium-high. Garlic 20 seconds. Bok choy cut-side down, 2 min. Splash of soy + 2 tbsp water, lid on, 2 min more.
  4. Plate greens, salmon on top, sesame seeds. Rice if you want it.

Tip: Miso burns fast. If your broiler's enthusiastic, drop the salmon a rack lower and watch it like you owe it money.

item.title: Thursday — Sicilian White Beans with Tuna, Lemon & Chili
item.description:
Serves 2. A 10-minute pantry dinner that punches way above its weight.

Ingredients

  • 1 × 400g can cannellini beans, drained (no-salt-added if available)
  • 1 × 150g can tuna in olive oil, drained (or in water)
  • 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (the good stuff)
  • 1 garlic clove, sliced wafer-thin
  • Pinch chili flakes
  • Zest and juice of 1 lemon
  • Big handful flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
  • Handful cherry tomatoes, halved (optional)
  • Couple of handfuls of arugula (optional)
  • Black pepper

Method

  1. Olive oil into a small pan over low heat. Garlic and chili flakes. Warm — not fry — for 2 min until the garlic just softens and smells sweet.
  2. Off the heat. Tip in the beans, stir gently to coat. Warm through.
  3. Into a bowl: beans, flaked tuna, lemon zest and juice, parsley, tomatoes if using.
  4. Toss. Black pepper. Skip the salt — taste first; the tuna and beans usually carry enough.
  5. Pile onto arugula or eat with a slice of whole-grain bread to mop the bowl.

Tip: Trick is good olive oil and not over-stirring — you want the tuna in chunks, not paste.

item.title: Friday — Thai Chicken Larb with Brown Rice
item.description:
Serves 2. Loud, sour, hot. Wake your mouth up.

Ingredients

  • 300g lean ground chicken (breast meat)
  • 2 tbsp jasmine or sticky rice (for toasted rice powder)
  • 2 shallots, sliced thin
  • 2 spring onions, sliced
  • 1–2 bird's eye chilies, finely sliced (calibrate to bravery)
  • Big handful fresh mint
  • Big handful cilantro
  • Dressing: 2 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp honey
  • Brown jasmine rice, to serve
  • Lettuce cups (optional, for wrapping)

Method

  1. Toasted rice powder first: dry-toast the rice in a small pan over medium until deep golden and nutty, 4–5 min. Cool, then grind in a mortar or blitz briefly. Texture of coarse sand.
  2. Same pan, no oil. Crumble in chicken over medium-high. Break it up small with a spoon. Cook 5–6 min until cooked through and starting to catch.
  3. Off the heat. Tip into a bowl. While warm: shallots, spring onions, chili, dressing, half the rice powder. Toss.
  4. Add the herbs last — torn, not chopped. Toss once.
  5. Pile over brown rice or into lettuce cups. Remaining rice powder on top.

Tip: The toasted rice powder is what makes it larb. Make extra and keep it in a jar — it's good on everything.

item.title: Monday — Red Lentil Dal with Wilted Spinach
item.description:
Serves 4. Freezes beautifully. A workhorse.

Ingredients

  • 250g red lentils, rinsed
  • 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 large onion, finely diced
  • 4 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
  • 1 tsp ground turmeric
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp ground coriander
  • ½ tsp chili powder (or to taste)
  • 1 × 400g can chopped tomatoes
  • 900ml low-sodium vegetable stock
  • 100g baby spinach
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • Small handful cilantro
  • Brown basmati rice or whole-wheat roti, to serve

Tadka: 1 tsp cumin seeds, ½ tsp mustard seeds, 1 dried red chili — bloomed in 1 tsp hot oil for 30 seconds

Method

  1. Oil in a large pot over medium. Onion until golden, 8–10 min. Add garlic and ginger, stir 1 min.
  2. Dry spices in. Stir 30 seconds. Tomatoes in. Cook 3 min until thickened and fragrant.
  3. Lentils and stock in. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook 20–25 min, stirring occasionally, until lentils are completely soft and collapsing.
  4. Stir in spinach — it wilts in 1 min. Squeeze lemon over. Taste and adjust salt.
  5. Make the tadka and drizzle over just before serving. Top with cilantro.

Tip: Dal thickens as it sits. Add a splash of water when reheating — it comes back perfectly.

item.title: Tuesday — Baked Mackerel with Roasted Tomatoes & Capers
item.description:
Serves 2. Mackerel is one of the best heart foods on the planet — omega-3 through the roof.

Ingredients

  • 2 whole mackerel, gutted and cleaned (or 4 fillets)
  • 300g cherry tomatoes
  • 2 tbsp capers, rinsed
  • 3 garlic cloves, sliced
  • 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 lemon, half sliced into rounds, half for juicing
  • Fresh thyme or oregano sprigs
  • Black pepper
  • Handful flat-leaf parsley, to finish
  • Whole-grain bread, to serve

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 200°C/390°F. Toss tomatoes, capers, and garlic with 1 tbsp olive oil. Spread in a roasting dish. Roast 15 min until blistered.
  2. Score the fish 3 times on each side. Stuff with lemon rounds and thyme. Nestle on top of the tomatoes. Drizzle remaining oil over fish.
  3. Roast 15–18 min until the flesh flakes away from the backbone easily.
  4. Squeeze lemon juice over everything. Scatter parsley. Eat with bread to mop the roasting juices.

Tip: Don't fear mackerel's boldness — the capers and tomatoes are exactly the right foil for it.

item.title: Wednesday — Black Bean Tacos with Mango Avocado Salsa
item.description:
Serves 2–3. Fully plant-based. Ready in 20 minutes.

Ingredients

  • 2 × 400g cans black beans, drained (no-salt-added)
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • Pinch chili flakes
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 6 small corn or whole-wheat tortillas
  • 1 small red cabbage, shredded
  • Lime juice, to dress cabbage

Salsa: 1 ripe mango (diced), 1 avocado (diced), ½ red onion (finely diced), 1 jalapeño (finely diced), juice of 2 limes, big handful cilantro, pinch salt

Method

  1. Make the salsa first: toss mango, avocado, onion, jalapeño, lime, and cilantro together. Set aside.
  2. Dress shredded cabbage with lime juice and a pinch of salt. Leave to soften slightly while you do everything else.
  3. Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high. Add beans and spices. Stir and cook 4–5 min until heated through and starting to crisp at the edges.
  4. Warm tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan.
  5. Build tacos: cabbage, beans, generous salsa on top.

Tip: Add the avocado to the salsa last so it doesn't go brown while you cook the beans.

item.title: Thursday — Baked Cod with Caponata
item.description:
Serves 2. Caponata is a Sicilian sweet-sour eggplant dish — make extra, it keeps 4 days in the fridge.

Ingredients

  • 2 cod fillets (~150g each), or any firm white fish
  • 1 tbsp olive oil + squeeze lemon
  • Black pepper and dried oregano

Caponata:

  • 1 large eggplant, cut into 2cm cubes
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 small onion, diced
  • 2 celery stalks, sliced
  • 1 × 400g can chopped tomatoes
  • 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
  • 1 tsp honey
  • 2 tbsp capers, rinsed
  • Handful green olives, pitted and roughly chopped
  • Handful flat-leaf parsley

Method

  1. Caponata: Salt the eggplant cubes, leave 10 min, then pat dry. Fry in olive oil over high heat until golden on all sides. Remove. Same pan: onion and celery, 5 min. Tomatoes, vinegar, honey in. Return eggplant. Simmer 15 min. Stir in capers and olives. Taste — should be sweet and sour. Parsley to finish.
  2. Preheat oven to 190°C. Rub cod with olive oil, lemon, black pepper, and oregano. Bake 12–15 min until it just flakes.
  3. Spoon caponata onto plates. Cod on top.

Tip: Caponata improves overnight. Make it ahead and the fish is a 15-minute dinner.

item.title: Friday — Korean-Style Ground Turkey Bowl (no egg)
item.description:
Serves 2. Fast, satisfying, and punchy. This is bibimbap energy without the egg.

Ingredients

  • 300g lean ground turkey (or chicken)
  • 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  • 1 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste)
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  • 1 tsp honey
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tsp grated ginger
  • Brown rice, to serve

Toppings: 1 cucumber (thinly sliced, dressed with rice vinegar + sesame oil + pinch sugar), 1 carrot (julienned), 2 spring onions (sliced), 1 tsp sesame seeds, handful baby spinach or sautéed beansprouts

Method

  1. Mix soy, gochujang, sesame oil, honey, garlic, and ginger into a sauce.
  2. Heat a pan over medium-high, no oil. Add turkey, break up with a spoon. Cook 5–6 min until browned through.
  3. Pour sauce over turkey. Stir and cook 1–2 min more until glossy and fragrant. Pull off heat.
  4. Dress cucumber. Prep other toppings.
  5. Build bowls: rice at the base, turkey alongside arranged toppings. Sesame seeds over everything.

Tip: The gochujang is the whole point. Don't skip it — it's deep and fruity, not just hot.

item.title: Monday — Turkish Red Lentil Soup (Mercimek Çorbası)
item.description:
Serves 4. Silky, warming, deeply satisfying. One of the great soups of the world.

Ingredients

  • 200g red lentils, rinsed
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, roughly chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves
  • 1 carrot, roughly chopped
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp paprika (sweet)
  • ½ tsp ground turmeric
  • 1 tbsp tomato paste
  • 1.2L low-sodium chicken or vegetable stock
  • Lemon wedges, to serve
  • Pinch dried mint + chili flakes + drizzle olive oil, to finish
  • Whole-wheat flatbread, to serve

Method

  1. Oil in a large pot over medium. Onion, garlic, carrot — soften 8 min. Spices and tomato paste in. Stir 1 min.
  2. Lentils and stock in. Bring to boil, reduce heat, simmer 20–25 min until lentils are completely soft.
  3. Blend until silky smooth. Return to pot. Thin with water if needed. Season gently.
  4. Ladle into bowls. Drizzle olive oil, sprinkle mint and chili flakes, big squeeze of lemon. Serve with flatbread.

Tip: The lemon at the end is mandatory — it lifts the whole soup from good to brilliant.

item.title: Tuesday — Grilled Chicken Thighs with Chimichurri & Roasted Peppers
item.description:
Serves 2. Chimichurri is one of the great sauces — bright, herby, acidic. Make extra.

Ingredients

  • 4 skinless chicken breasts (~600g), lightly pounded to even thickness
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika, olive oil, black pepper — for the rub
  • 2 red bell peppers, halved and deseeded
  • Olive oil for peppers

Chimichurri: Large bunch flat-leaf parsley (stalks and all), 4 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp dried oregano, ½ tsp chili flakes, 80ml extra virgin olive oil, pinch salt

Method

  1. Make chimichurri: blitz everything together briefly — you want texture, not a purée. Or chop by hand for a chunkier version. Let it sit 20 min for the flavors to open up.
  2. Toss peppers with olive oil. Grill or roast at 220°C until softened and charred in spots, ~20 min.
  3. Rub chicken with paprika, olive oil, and pepper. Grill over medium-high: 5–6 min per side until cooked through (internal temp 74°C/165°F). Rest 5 min before slicing.
  4. Plate chicken and peppers. Spoon chimichurri generously over. Extra on the side.

Tip: Chimichurri keeps for a week in the fridge under a thin layer of oil. Use it on everything.

item.title: Wednesday — Sardinian-Style Minestrone with Farro
item.description:
Serves 4–6. Farro gives this soup a nutty chew regular minestrone lacks. A pot of longevity food.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 onion, diced
  • 2 carrots, diced
  • 3 celery stalks, diced
  • 4 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tsp dried rosemary
  • 1 × 400g can chopped tomatoes
  • 1 × 400g can borlotti or cannellini beans, drained
  • 150g pearled farro (or spelt), rinsed
  • 1.5L low-sodium vegetable stock
  • 150g cavolo nero (Tuscan kale) or regular kale, stems removed, torn
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • Good extra virgin olive oil, to drizzle
  • Black pepper

Method

  1. Olive oil in a large pot over medium. Onion, carrot, celery — cook low and slow, 10 min, until truly soft.
  2. Garlic and rosemary in. 1 min. Tomatoes in. Cook 5 min.
  3. Beans, farro, and stock in. Bring to boil, reduce to simmer. Cook 25 min until farro is tender.
  4. Stir in kale. Cook 5 min more. Squeeze lemon in. Taste and season.
  5. Ladle into deep bowls. Drizzle of good olive oil, black pepper. That's it.

Tip: Farro absorbs a lot of stock overnight — add more water when reheating. The soup only gets better.

item.title: Thursday — Spiced Turkey Kofta with Tabbouleh
item.description:
Serves 2–3. The kofta take 5 min to mix. The tabbouleh is the work, and it's worth it.

Ingredients

Kofta:

  • 350g lean ground turkey (breast mince)
  • 1 small onion, grated (squeeze out excess water)
  • 2 garlic cloves, grated
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp ground coriander
  • ½ tsp cinnamon
  • ½ tsp chili flakes
  • Small handful flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
  • Black pepper

Tabbouleh:

  • 100g bulgur wheat
  • Large bunch flat-leaf parsley (mostly leaf, some stem), very finely chopped
  • Small bunch fresh mint, very finely chopped
  • 4 spring onions, finely sliced
  • 3 medium ripe tomatoes, deseeded and finely diced
  • 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • 3 tbsp lemon juice
  • Salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Soak bulgur in just-boiled water for 15 min. Drain and squeeze dry in a clean cloth. Cool.
  2. Mix kofta ingredients. Shape into 8–10 oval patties around skewers or just as free-form patties. Chill 10 min if time allows.
  3. Combine all tabbouleh ingredients. Parsley should dominate — this is a herb salad, not a grain salad. Taste, season, toss.
  4. Grill or pan-fry kofta over high heat, 3–4 min per side until nicely charred and cooked through.
  5. Serve kofta on a bed of tabbouleh. A wedge of lemon.

Tip: Real tabbouleh is 70% herb, 30% everything else. Most people get this backwards.

item.title: Friday — Ginger-Soy Baked Trout with Sesame Soba Noodles
item.description:
Serves 2. Soba noodles are 100% buckwheat if you can find them — more fiber, better flavor.

Ingredients

  • 2 rainbow trout fillets (~150g each)
  • Marinade: 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 tsp honey, 1 tsp toasted sesame oil, 1 garlic clove (grated)
  • 150g soba noodles (100% buckwheat if possible)
  • 1 tbsp tahini
  • 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  • 1 tbsp rice vinegar
  • 1 tsp sesame oil
  • 1 tsp honey
  • 2–3 tbsp water to thin
  • 4 radishes, thinly sliced
  • ½ cucumber, halved and thinly sliced
  • 2 spring onions, sliced
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds

Method

  1. Mix marinade. Brush over trout. Set aside 15 min while oven heats to 200°C.
  2. Bake trout on a lined tray 10–12 min until just cooked through and a little caramelized at the edges.
  3. Cook soba per packet — usually 4–5 min. Drain, rinse under cold water immediately (stops them going gluey).
  4. Whisk tahini dressing. Toss cold soba with dressing, radish, cucumber, and spring onion.
  5. Pile noodles in bowls. Lay trout on top. Sesame seeds over everything.

Tip: Rinse soba cold immediately after draining — non-negotiable, otherwise they clump into one sad mass.

item.title: Monday — Silken Tofu & Bok Choy Stir-Fry with Ginger-Sesame Sauce
item.description:
Serves 2. Tofu is one of the most effective dietary interventions for LDL cholesterol. This one is actually delicious.

Ingredients

  • 400g firm tofu, pressed and cut into 2cm cubes
  • 2 tbsp cornstarch (for coating)
  • 1 tbsp neutral oil
  • 3 heads baby bok choy, halved lengthwise
  • 3 garlic cloves, sliced
  • 1 tbsp fresh ginger, finely grated
  • 3 spring onions, cut into 3cm lengths
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
  • Brown rice, to serve

Sauce: 2 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp honey, 1 tsp cornstarch, 3 tbsp water, pinch chili flakes

Method

  1. Press tofu between paper towels for 10 min. Toss cubes in cornstarch. Mix sauce in a small bowl and set aside.
  2. Heat oil in a wide non-stick pan over high heat. Add tofu in a single layer. Don't touch for 3 min until the bottom side is golden and crisp. Flip. Another 2 min. Remove and set aside.
  3. Same pan, still hot. Bok choy cut-side down. Char 2 min. Add garlic and ginger — 30 seconds. Spring onions in.
  4. Return tofu. Pour sauce over. Toss everything together — it will thicken almost immediately. 1 min max.
  5. Pile over brown rice. Sesame seeds over the top.

Tip: Press the tofu properly — wet tofu steams instead of crisping. Ten minutes with a heavy pan on top is all it takes.

item.title: Tuesday — Harissa-Spiced Cauliflower & Chickpea Couscous
item.description:
Serves 2–3. Roasting does something profound to cauliflower. Don't rush it — let it char.

Ingredients

  • 1 small head cauliflower, cut into florets
  • 1 × 400g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
  • 2 tbsp harissa paste
  • 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 200g whole-wheat couscous
  • 250ml just-boiled low-sodium vegetable stock (for couscous)
  • Zest and juice of 1 lemon
  • Big handful flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
  • Small handful fresh mint, roughly chopped
  • 2 tbsp toasted flaked almonds (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 220°C. Toss cauliflower and chickpeas with harissa, olive oil, and cumin. Spread in a single layer on a large baking tray — crowding kills the char.
  2. Roast 25–30 min, turning halfway, until cauliflower has dark edges and chickpeas are crispy in places.
  3. Meanwhile: couscous into a bowl, pour over hot stock, cover with a plate, leave 5 min. Fluff with a fork. Stir in lemon zest, a squeeze of lemon, and the herbs.
  4. Pile couscous into bowls. Top with roasted cauliflower and chickpeas. Extra lemon juice over. Almonds if using.

Tip: The chickpeas at the edges of the tray will be almost chip-like. Fight over them.

item.title: Wednesday — Teriyaki Salmon Bowl with Pickled Cucumber & Brown Rice
item.description:
Serves 2. The pickled cucumber is what makes this. Don't skip it — it takes 5 minutes and cuts right through the salmon's richness.

Ingredients

  • 2 salmon fillets (~150g each), skin-on

Teriyaki glaze: 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tbsp mirin (or ½ tsp honey + splash of rice vinegar), ½ tsp toasted sesame oil, 1 tsp grated ginger

Quick pickled cucumber: 1 cucumber (halved, deseeded, thinly sliced), 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp honey, pinch chili flakes, ½ tsp sesame oil

  • Brown rice, cooked, to serve
  • 2 spring onions, finely sliced
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
  • Handful edamame (frozen, thawed) — optional

Method

  1. Combine cucumber, rice vinegar, honey, chili flakes, and sesame oil. Toss and set aside — it softens as it sits.
  2. Mix teriyaki glaze. Pat salmon dry. Brush glaze on the flesh side.
  3. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high. Salmon skin-down. Press lightly for 1 min to stop curling. Cook 4–5 min until the skin is crisp. Flip. 1–2 min on the flesh side — it should still be slightly rare in the center.
  4. Build bowls: rice, pickled cucumber, edamame if using. Salmon on top. Spring onions and sesame seeds. Any remaining glaze drizzled over.

Tip: Don't move the salmon while the skin cooks. Leave it alone and it'll release cleanly when ready.

item.title: Thursday — Chicken Saag (Spinach Curry, No Cream)
item.description:
Serves 3–4. The restaurant version is mostly cream. This one is mostly spinach — better for you and, honestly, better tasting.

Ingredients

  • 500g skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
  • 1 tbsp neutral oil
  • 1 large onion, finely diced
  • 4 garlic cloves, grated
  • 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp ground coriander
  • 1 tsp garam masala
  • ½ tsp ground turmeric
  • ½ tsp chili powder (adjust to heat preference)
  • 1 × 400g can chopped tomatoes
  • 200g baby spinach (or 400g regular spinach, stems removed)
  • 100ml low-sodium chicken stock or water
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • Small handful cilantro
  • Brown basmati rice or whole-wheat roti, to serve

Method

  1. Oil over medium-high. Chicken pieces in — brown on all sides, 4–5 min. Remove and set aside.
  2. Same pan over medium. Onion until golden, 8–10 min. Garlic and ginger in — 1 min. All dry spices in — 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
  3. Tomatoes in. Cook 5 min until the sauce thickens and oil starts to separate at the edges.
  4. Return chicken plus the stock. Simmer 10–12 min covered until chicken is cooked through.
  5. Add spinach in large handfuls, stir until wilted, 2–3 min. Squeeze lemon over. Taste and season. Scatter cilantro.

Tip: The sauce should look a little dry when you add the spinach — spinach throws out a lot of water. Don't panic and don't add extra liquid.

item.title: Friday — Thai Peanut Noodles with Edamame & Shredded Carrot
item.description:
Serves 2. Served cold or at room temperature. This is Friday food — minimal cooking, maximum satisfaction.

Ingredients

  • 200g soba noodles or rice noodles
  • 150g frozen edamame, defrosted
  • 2 medium carrots, julienned or coarsely grated
  • ½ red cabbage, finely shredded (about 150g)
  • 3 spring onions, sliced
  • Big handful cilantro
  • 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
  • 1 bird's eye chili, thinly sliced (optional)

Peanut sauce: 3 tbsp natural peanut butter (no added sugar), 2 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce, 2 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp toasted sesame oil, 1 tsp honey, 1 garlic clove (grated), 1 tsp grated ginger, 3–4 tbsp water to thin

Method

  1. Cook noodles per packet. Drain, rinse under cold water. Shake dry.
  2. Whisk peanut sauce. It will look seized initially — keep whisking, it comes together. Add water until it's a pourable dressing consistency.
  3. Combine noodles, edamame, carrot, cabbage, and spring onion in a large bowl. Pour sauce over and toss thoroughly.
  4. Plate up. Cilantro, sesame seeds, and chili on top. Extra lime wedge on the side.

Tip: Make extra sauce. It keeps 5 days in the fridge and improves everything it touches — grilled chicken, roasted veg, steamed greens.

item.title: Monday — Tuna & White Bean Niçoise Salad (No Egg)
item.description:
Serves 2. The classic Niçoise, minus the egg, plus beans for extra heft. Better, honestly.

Ingredients

  • 2 × 120g cans tuna in olive oil, drained (keep 1 tbsp of the oil)
  • 1 × 400g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
  • 200g green beans, trimmed
  • 200g cherry tomatoes, halved
  • ½ red onion, very thinly sliced
  • 2 tbsp capers, rinsed
  • Handful black olives (Niçoise or Kalamata), pitted
  • Big handful flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
  • 2 Little Gem lettuces or 1 head Romaine, leaves separated

Dressing: 1 tbsp reserved tuna oil, 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, pinch chili flakes, black pepper

Method

  1. Blanch green beans in boiling water 3 min. Drain. Immediately plunge into cold water to keep them bright. Drain again.
  2. Soak red onion slices in cold water for 10 min to take the raw edge off. Drain.
  3. Whisk dressing. Taste — should be punchy.
  4. Arrange lettuce on a platter. Layer over beans, cherry tomatoes, green beans, onion, capers, and olives. Flake tuna in large chunks over the top — don't break it up too much. Scatter parsley.
  5. Drizzle dressing over at the table, not before. Serve immediately.

Tip: Good tuna (in olive oil, not water) and good olives make or break this. Don't dress too early or everything wilts.

item.title: Tuesday — Ground Turkey & Farro Stuffed Peppers
item.description:
Serves 2–4 (makes 4 halves). Meal-preps brilliantly. Reheat in the oven at 180°C for 15 min.

Ingredients

  • 2 large red or yellow bell peppers, halved lengthwise, seeds removed
  • 300g lean ground turkey
  • 150g pearled farro, cooked (about 350g cooked weight)
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 small onion, finely diced
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • ½ tsp dried oregano
  • 1 × 400g can chopped tomatoes
  • Handful flat-leaf parsley, chopped
  • Black pepper
  • Lemon wedges, to serve

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 200°C. Brush pepper halves with a little olive oil. Roast cut-side up 15 min while you make the filling.
  2. Oil in a pan over medium-high. Onion until soft, 5 min. Garlic in, 1 min. Turkey in — break it up and cook until browned, 6–7 min.
  3. Spices in. Stir 30 seconds. Add half the can of tomatoes (save the rest for a sauce or another night). Cook 3 min until thickened.
  4. Off the heat. Stir in cooked farro and most of the parsley. Taste and season.
  5. Spoon filling generously into roasted pepper halves, mounding it up. Return to oven 15 min until the tops start to catch.
  6. Remaining parsley over the top. Lemon wedge on the side.

Tip: Farro's nuttiness works better here than rice — don't substitute if you can help it.

item.title: Wednesday — Spaghetti with Sardines, Capers & Chili
item.description:
Serves 2. Sardines are one of the highest omega-3 foods on earth, cheap as anything, and this Sicilian pasta is one of the most underrated weeknight dinners in existence.

Ingredients

  • 200g whole-wheat spaghetti or linguine
  • 2 × 120g cans sardines in olive oil, drained (keep 1 tbsp oil)
  • 4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
  • ½–1 tsp chili flakes (to taste)
  • 2 tbsp capers, rinsed
  • Handful green olives, pitted and roughly chopped (optional)
  • Zest and juice of 1 lemon
  • 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • Big handful flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
  • Black pepper
  • 2 tbsp toasted breadcrumbs (whole-wheat, optional — sub for Parmesan, which you're skipping)

Method

  1. Cook pasta in a large pot of well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 100ml pasta water before draining.
  2. While pasta cooks: in a wide pan over low heat, warm olive oil and sardine oil together. Add garlic and chili flakes. Slow-cook 3 min — don't rush this, the garlic should be pale gold and sweet, not brown and bitter.
  3. Add sardines. Break them up gently with a wooden spoon — you want chunks, not mush. Capers and olives in. 1 min.
  4. Drained pasta into the pan. Toss. Splash in pasta water as needed to loosen. Lemon zest and juice over. Parsley in. Toss again.
  5. Plate. Toasted breadcrumbs over the top for crunch. Extra lemon, extra chili if you want it.

Tip: The breadcrumbs do the job Parmesan normally does — crunch, salt, savory depth. Don't skip them.

item.title: Thursday — Roasted Vegetable & Lentil Traybake
item.description:
Serves 2–3. Everything on one tray. The lentils soak up the roasting juices. One of those recipes that's less than the sum of its parts until it isn't.

Ingredients

  • 1 red bell pepper, cut into chunks
  • 1 medium eggplant, cut into 3cm cubes
  • 1 medium zucchini, cut into 3cm chunks
  • 1 red onion, cut into wedges
  • 3 garlic cloves, left whole in skin
  • 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 tsp smoked paprika
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 × 400g can green or brown lentils, drained and rinsed
  • 1 × 400g can chopped tomatoes
  • 100ml low-sodium vegetable stock or water
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • Big handful flat-leaf parsley
  • Whole-grain bread, to serve

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 210°C. Toss eggplant, pepper, zucchini, and onion with olive oil, paprika, and cumin. Spread across a large roasting dish. Tuck in the garlic cloves. Roast 20 min until softened and starting to colour.
  2. Pull the tray out. Squeeze the garlic out of its skin and mash into the vegetables. Add the lentils, tomatoes, and stock. Stir to combine. Return to oven for 20 min more — the tomatoes should thicken and the lentils absorb the liquid.
  3. Squeeze lemon over. Scatter parsley. Check seasoning.
  4. Bring the tray to the table. Eat with good bread to mop the juices.

Tip: Don't use canned red lentils here — they'll dissolve into mush. Green or brown lentils hold their shape through the roast.

item.title: Friday — Miso Ramen with Tofu, Bok Choy & Mushrooms
item.description:
Serves 2. This is not instant ramen. This is a 25-minute bowl that tastes like it took three hours.

Ingredients

Broth:

  • 1L low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock
  • 3 tbsp white miso paste
  • 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger
  • 1 tsp gochujang or chili paste (optional, for heat)

Bowl:

  • 200g ramen noodles (or soba as a substitute)
  • 200g firm tofu, cut into 1cm slabs
  • 150g shiitake or chestnut mushrooms, sliced
  • 2 heads baby bok choy, halved
  • 2 spring onions, finely sliced
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
  • 1 tsp neutral oil
  • Sheet of nori (dried seaweed), torn — optional

Method

  1. Press tofu briefly. Heat oil in a non-stick pan over high. Tofu slabs in — 2–3 min per side until golden. Set aside.
  2. Same pan: mushrooms over high heat, no stirring for 2 min until they colour. Season with a splash of soy. Set aside.
  3. Blanch bok choy in boiling water 1 min. Drain.
  4. For the broth: gently heat stock over medium. Whisk in miso (never boil miso — it kills the probiotics and dulls the flavour). Add soy, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and gochujang if using. Taste — it should be deeply savoury.
  5. Cook noodles per packet. Drain.
  6. Divide noodles between deep bowls. Ladle over hot broth. Arrange tofu, mushrooms, and bok choy. Spring onions, sesame seeds, and nori on top.

Tip: Never boil miso broth. Bring the stock to temperature, pull it off the heat, then whisk the miso in. The difference is real.
